title: Termination and Payoff Closure of Operating Lines of Credit
content:
An active line of the Operating Lines of Credit is terminated only at the member's own instruction; a matured line is closed by the servicing platform once it is paid in full.

## Termination clause

1. **Member's instruction.** An active line is terminated only at the member's own instruction: the request is registered as a line closure request, and the termination takes effect when the member confirms it.
2. **Request on file.** An active line may be closed only when the member has a line closure request on file for that line, as the association's service request records show for that same line.
3. **Nothing owed.** It may be closed only when outstanding principal, accrued interest and fees due are all 0.00, including the final accrual through the payoff date booked under the interest billing rules and paid.
4. **Zero balance alone.** A zero balance alone never closes an active line before maturity.
5. **Matured line.** A matured line is closed by the servicing platform on the effective date of the payment that brings principal, interest and fees to zero.
6. **Lien release.** After closure the association files a UCC termination statement within 20 calendar days of the closed date, unless another line or loan of the member is secured by the same financing statement.
7. **No refund.** No origination, renewal or other fee is refunded on closure.

## Closure judgement for an active line

| Line closure request on file for the line | Principal, interest and fees all 0.00, final accrual paid | Member confirms | Closed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | Yes | — | No |
| Yes | No | — | No |

## Lien release example (hypothetical dates)

A line closed on 3 March whose financing statement secures nothing else has its UCC termination statement filed no later than 23 March, 20 calendar days after the closed date. If the member's Seasonal Operating Loan is secured by the same financing statement, no termination statement is filed.
